extracted.intended_audience: individual humanities scholars applying for NEH Fellowships (including independent scholars, junior scholars, and translators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for individual applicants seeking NEH Fellowships to support humanities research, writing, translations, editions, or born-digital projects. Covers eligibility, required application components, formatting, review criteria, and administrative policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 1: Intellectual significance of the proposed project
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual significance of the proposed project, including its value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the project's basic ideas, problems, or questions; state the thesis/claim(s); explain how the project complements, challenges, or expands relevant studies; discuss how the scholarship will be presented to benefit intended audiences. For translations, justify a new translation if other English translations exist; if the final product will be in a language other than English, explain rationale and implications for access. Narrative section 'Significance and contribution' (part of Attachment 1) addresses this criterion and is primarily considered under review criterion 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 2: Quality of conception, definition, organization, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project and the applicant’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain theoretical framework, concepts, terminology, methods, and sources. For publications, describe final product organization (books: chapter outline if possible; born-digital: outline of major elements and technologies/platforms; editions/translations: scholarly apparatus). For dissertation revisions, explain how the project moves beyond the dissertation. Narrative heading 'Organization, concepts, and methods' aligns primarily with this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 3: Feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed work plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed work plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a schedule for the period of performance in increments of three months or fewer (narrative or table). Indicate current state of project and tasks to accomplish. Work plan must be based on full-time commitment, reflect major narrative activities and project dates, avoid heavy dependence on factors beyond applicant control (e.g., outside reviewers' reports), include location(s) and time spent at each, and explain timeline if project not completed during period. The work plan is Attachment 2, limited to one page, and will be considered primarily under review criterion 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 4: Quality or promise of quality of the applicant as an interpreter of the humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality or promise of quality of the applicant as an interpreter of the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate competence/background, level of language/technology/method skills, access to archives/collections, and relevant arrangements. The résumé/CV (Attachment 4) should list positions, education (degrees, dates, thesis/dissertation titles), awards/honors (with dates), prior NEH support and resulting products, publications, and other relevant activities including language and digital competencies. Bibliography (Attachment 3) evidences subject-area knowledge; both components are evaluated primarily under criterion 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion 5: Likelihood of project completion and soundness of dissemination/access plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood that the applicant will complete the project (not necessarily during the period of performance), including, when relevant, the soundness of the dissemination and access plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intended results, identify intended audience, explain dissemination means and why appropriate, provide URLs if applicable, address copyright permission plans where necessary. NEH prefers projects that provide free public access; peer-reviewed articles must comply with NEH Public Access Policy. Data management plans and preservation strategies affect this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative content and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for Attachment 1: Narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative must be succinct, well organized, free of jargon, single-spaced, no more than three pages. Do not include executive summary, cover page, or table of contents. Images/charts/footnotes/endnotes are allowed if within page limit. Organize using specified headings (Significance and contribution; Organization, concepts, and methods; Competencies, skills, and access; Final product and dissemination). Narrative will be considered primarily under review criteria 1, 2, 4, and 5. Name file narrative.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work plan attachment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment 2: Work plan content and constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One page maximum. Present schedule in ≤3-month increments; describe current state and tasks; base plan on full-time commitment; do not include chapter outline (chapter outlines belong in the narrative); include locations and durations. Explain reliance on prior NEH Summer Stipend accomplishments if applicable. Work plan primarily considered under review criterion 3. Name file workplan.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment 3: Bibliography expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One page maximum. Include primary and secondary sources most directly related to the project (substance and theoretical/methodological approaches). Evaluators use bibliography to assess familiarity with the field. Any standard bibliographic format is acceptable. Name file bibliography.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Résumé/CV requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment 4: Résumé/CV content and page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two pages maximum. Do not submit narrative biographical statement. Include name, current and past positions, education (degrees, dates, and thesis/dissertation titles), awards/honors (with dates), publications (full citations), professional activities, and competencies in languages and digital tools. Indicate prior NEH support and resulting products. Name file resume.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editions and translations sample requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment 5: If creating an edition or translation, provide sample materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide one page of the original text and one page of the edited/translated version (two pages total). If including annotations, include examples in the sample. Do not exceed two pages total. Sample considered primarily under review criterion 2. Name file translation.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual materials and data sample guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments 6 and 7: Visual materials and data sample recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual materials: recommended, PDF format (not .jpg), up to one page. Data sample: recommended for datasets, up to one page. Visual materials primarily considered under review criterion 2; data sample under criterion 2. Name files visual.pdf and data.pdf respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and sharing plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment 8: Data management and sharing plan conditional requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two pages maximum. Describe plan for hosting, maintaining, and preserving digital products; who is responsible during active maintenance; standards for data/metadata formats; data security and confidentiality measures; plans for preservation after active maintenance and what elements will be preserved. Considered under review criteria 2 and 5. Name file datamanagement.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirements and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH requests two letters of reference and specifies expectations for their content and submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names, emails, and affiliations on supplemental form. Ideally letters come from different institutions. Letters should address the review criteria with reference to the specific project and are more highly regarded if they consider the specific proposed activity and attest to the candidate’s ability. For translations, one letter should be from a language expert addressing the one-page translation sample. NEH will email letter writers ~2–3 weeks after deadline and accepts letters after the deadline (late letters may not be considered). Missing letters will not disqualify an application. Elected officials, NEH staff, and current National Council members may not serve as letter writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Citizenship, residency, and student status
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may apply to the Fellowships program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible: U.S. citizens (domestic or abroad) and foreign nationals who have lived in the U.S. or jurisdictions for at least the three years prior to the application deadline. Foreign nationals who take up permanent residence outside the U.S. between application deadline and end of period forfeit eligibility; temporary travel abroad is permitted. Currently enrolled students are eligible only if they have satisfied degree requirements and are awaiting conferral and include Attachment 9: Degree conferral (letter from dean/chair). Organizations are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission, multiple submissions, and concurrent NEH application limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on submitting multiple or related applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may revise and resubmit previously rejected applications; submissions are subject to current competition requirements. You may submit only one application under this notice; if multiple submissions occur, NEH accepts only your last validated submission prior to the deadline under the correct funding opportunity. You may apply to only one of certain named NEH programs in a fiscal year (list provided). Projects previously funded by certain NEH programs are ineligible for this funding (list provided). If you accept an NEH Fellowship, pending Summer Stipends, Public Scholars, or DLI applications for the same project will be automatically withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance and full-time work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing and commitment requirements for the award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request between six and twelve months, start between Jan 1, 2026 and Sep 1, 2027; period must be continuous, start on first day of month and end on last day. During period, must work full time on project and forego teaching, administrative assignments, and other major activities. Requesting shorter period does not improve chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and stipend calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipend rate and award minimum/maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH provides $5,000 per month for full-time work. Minimum award $30,000 for six months; maximum $60,000 for twelve months. Amount depends on number of months requested. Awards are outright funds (no matching) and indirect costs are unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment and file formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical formatting requirements for attachments and page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments must be single PDF files. Page size: standard letter (8.5"x11"). At least one-inch margins on all sides. Font size no smaller than 11-point. Standard Roman fonts (Arial, Georgia, Helvetica, Times New Roman). Single-spacing. Any standard citation style acceptable; citations included in page counts. Do not include attachments other than requested; NEH will reject applications with extra attachments. Page limits for fellowships are mandatory; applications exceeding page limits or deviating from formatting instructions will not be reviewed. Specific filenames are requested (narrative.pdf, workplan.pdf, bibliography.pdf, resume.pdf, translation.pdf, visual.pdf, data.pdf, datamanagement.pdf, degreeconferral.pdf, delinquentdebt.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title and project description guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on what to enter for project title and description on SF-424.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title: brief (≤125 characters), descriptive and understandable to general public; avoid reliance on subtitle. NEH may retitle funded projects for clarity. Project description: write for non-specialist, state importance and relation to larger humanities issues, ≤1,000 characters including spaces; exceeding limit may cause Grants.gov to reject or truncate description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited projects and funding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of activities and projects NEH will not fund under this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will not fund: research by students enrolled in degree programs (including dissertations), preparation/revision of textbooks, development of curricula/teaching methods/theories, educational/language/technical impact assessments, graphic novels/graphic nonfiction, writing books for children or young adults, fiction, inventories of collections, guidebooks/how-to/self-help books, creation/production of documentary films, promotion of a particular political/religious/ideological POV, advocacy of a program of social/political action, projects outside the humanities (creation/performance of art), creative writing/autobiography/memoir/creative nonfiction, policy studies, and social science research that does not address humanistic questions or use humanistic methods. Awards to individuals: indirect costs unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness, submission platform, and registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements for submission and consequences for missing steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply using Grants.gov Workspace; complete multistep registration (Grants.gov, login.gov, SAM.gov) — ensure registration and password current; NEH will not grant deadline extensions for lack of registration. Complete all required and conditionally required components; NEH will not review applications missing required documents. Contact fellowships@neh.gov for paper copy requests. NEH may reject files that do not meet Grants.gov file requirements. NEH accepts letters after the deadline but they may not be considered; missing reference letters will not disqualify an application. Except rare late-submission policy cases, NEH will not consider late applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters timing, notification, and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: How NEH solicits and tracks letters of reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately two to three weeks after the deadline, NEH will email letter writers with instructions and they should submit letters online by the specified due date (e.g., May 7, 2025). Applicants are responsible for ensuring letter writers receive and respond; NEH will notify applicant by email when each letter is received. Applicants can check status in NEH secure area using application number and Grants.gov tracking number and can send reminders (including upload link) from that site. If letter writers must be changed after deadline contact fellowships@neh.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for public access and copyright/acknowledgment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH policy on public access to award products and intellectual property rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH strives to make award products available to the broadest audience and gives preference to projects providing free public access. Projects that produce peer-reviewed articles must follow NEH Public Access Policy. Subject to law, awardees may copyright work developed, but NEH reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce/publish/use the work for federal purposes and require recipients to make works available per Public Access Policy. Materials publicizing or products resulting from NEH-funded activities must acknowledge NEH support; consult Acknowledgment and Publicity Requirements for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of risk and pre-award compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH pre-award risk assessment and compliance checks for selected applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Chair's selection, NEH Office of Grant Management conducts risk assessment considering past performance, eligibility, and public policy compliance. OGM may request additional programmatic/administrative information or activities in anticipation of award. NEH may impose special terms or decline to issue awards for applicants with management/financial instability. Award decisions are discretionary and not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delinquent federal debt and debarment/suspension certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification requirements related to debarment, suspension, and delinquent federal debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must certify they are not debarred/suspended/declared ineligible and have not been convicted of certain offenses in the prior three years. NEH will not process awards for individuals with delinquent federal debt or who are debarred. If you cannot attest, explain in Attachment 10 (Explanation of delinquent federal debt) and provide evidence of repayment arrangements. NEH may require this information from recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation revision eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for applicants proposing projects based on completed dissertations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may seek funding for a project based on a completed dissertation but must state in the narrative that you intend to revise it and explain how the proposed project moves beyond the original. Address overlap with prior NEH Summer Stipend work if applicable; NEH will not support work already completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative projects and individual award limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for collaborative work under an individual-focused program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is designed for individual researchers; awards may not be divided. If funding more than one scholar in a collaborative project, each individual must submit a separate application specifying their individual contribution and independently meet eligibility requirements, and clearly explain division of labor and interdependence. Applicants working as part of a collaborative team but seeking funding only for themselves are eligible; collaborating scholars at eligible institutions should consider the Collaborative Research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of federal entities and ineligibility if project mirrors federal activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions when projects are closely tied to federal entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH does not issue awards to other federal entities. If project is so closely intertwined with a federal entity that it takes on characteristics of that entity’s authorized activities, it is ineligible. You may use funds, sites, or materials controlled by federal entities in your project, but not receive awards if project essentially performs federal entity functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting personal identifiable information (PII) and survey consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for handling PII and participant consent in NEH-funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients collecting PII are responsible for protecting and storing it, taking reasonable measures to prevent disclosure or loss; NEH is not liable for inadvertent disclosure. If collecting PII, discuss safeguarding plans in data management plan. If project includes surveys, obtain legally informed consent before enrolling participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and closeout requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award reporting expectations for Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a final performance report within 120 calendar days after period ends via eGMS Reach, including accomplishments, outputs, other financial support, impact, and NEH acknowledgement. Final financial report is not required. Projects producing peer-reviewed articles must follow Public Access Policy. NEH encourages sending copies of books resulting from NEH support to the Division of Research and updating products/prizes in eGMS Reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application time estimate and PRA notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time burden to prepare application and PRA contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH estimates on average 60 hours to complete an application (reviewing instructions, gathering information, completing and reviewing application). Comments on estimated completion time or other aspects may be sent to the PRA Officer at pra@neh.gov.
